inline_comments.comment: "the ASE's" is grammatically awkward. Should be "ASE's" (drop the article): "which can read all the same file formats that ASE's :func:`~ase.io.read` function understands:".

The phrase "the atoms that are open in a Python session" is ambiguous — it could be read as atoms currently displayed in an open GUI window, rather than the atoms object held in a variable. The old wording was clearer: "to keep changes to your atoms". Consider something like: "To make changes that propagate back to the `atoms` variable in the Python session, use `atoms.edit()` instead."

The underline character was changed from `---` to `...`, but this is the *first* heading character encountered after the page title (`===`). Sphinx/RST assigns heading levels in order of first appearance, so `...` will be established as the level-1 section style and `---` (used from "Basic controls" onward) will become level-2. This causes every subsequent section — "Basic controls", "Plotting data from the command line", "Configuring the GUI", and "Polling the GUI" — to render as subsections *of* "Selecting a part of a trajectory", which is structurally wrong. Change the underline back to `---` to match all other section headings in this file.

The old documentation had a "Writing files" section documenting the `-o` flag and the list of supported output formats (`traj`, `xyz`, `cube`, `pdb`, `eps`, `png`, `pov`). This has been removed without being relocated anywhere. Users who want to know how to export a trajectory to a different format from the command line (e.g., `ase gui -n -1 a*.traj -o new.traj`) now have nowhere to find this. Either restore the section here or move it to a relevant place in the docs.
Line 6 is a whitespace-only line inside the `.. attention::` block. This trailing whitespace is a CI lint failure risk and should be removed, leaving only a blank line.

The label listed here is "Magnetic moment" (singular), but the updated `gui.py` uses `_('_Magnetic moments')` (plural). The docs should match the actual menu text. Similarly on line 56, "Initial charge" should be "Initial charges" (plural, matching `_('_Initial charges')` in gui.py).
The label is listed as "Chemical symbol", but the menu item in the updated `gui.py` reads `_('_Element symbol')`. The docs should use the actual menu label "Element symbol" for consistency.
Trailing whitespace at the end of the line after "create the ". The line should end with "the" and a newline, with no trailing space. This will fail lint CI checks.
Duplicate word: "These constraints will be then be saved" should be "These constraints will then be saved".

Lines 119–121 contain the NEB command example wrapped in RST comments (`.. ::` / `..   $`), making them invisible in the rendered documentation. If the command (`ase gui --interpolate 3 initial.xyz final.xyz -o interpolated_path.traj`) is valid and useful, it should be in an actual `::` code block so readers can see it. If it is no longer the recommended workflow, the comment should be removed entirely rather than left as hidden dead text.

"Interface to :func:`ase.eos.plot`" is both very terse and potentially incorrect as a cross-reference: `plot` is an instance method on `EquationOfState`, not a standalone module-level function, so `:func:`ase.eos.plot`` may not resolve correctly in Sphinx. Consider linking to `:class:`ase.eos.EquationOfState`` and adding a brief note about what input the Bulk Modulus tool expects (e.g., a series of images at different volumes).
Typo: "Depending on you operating system" should be "Depending on your operating system".

general_comments.comment: The PR makes good progress documenting previously undocumented menu items across Edit, View, and Tools, and the overall reorganization of basics.rst is an improvement. The most urgent fix needed before merge is the RST heading hierarchy regression in basics.rst (the `...` underline on "Selecting a part of a trajectory"), as it will cause the entire lower portion of that page to render at the wrong level in the output.

The keyboard shortcut names in the new documentation use mixed conventions: some sections write `:kbd:`ctrl+Z`` (lowercase), others write `:kbd:`Ctrl+E`` (titlecase). For consistency, pick one convention throughout all the new `.rst` files. Lowercase (`:kbd:`ctrl+z``) is common in modern web documentation and matches what is already present in the older portions of these files.
